unit.why: A short anecdote, quoted from another book, in which a man asks R. Zusya to teach him awe and the rebbe makes him fall to the ground with a gesture of his hand.
unit.boundary_note: Part of a thematic anthology on awe: the previous division is also a Zusya awe anecdote, and the next is a homily on awe.

stories.start_quote: וכמו ששאל אחד את הה״צ מו״ר
stories.summary_en: A man asks R. Zusya to teach him to serve God in awe; when the rebbe lowers his hand the man falls on his face from overwhelming awe and cannot rise until the rebbe raises his hand again.

quotes: ולא יכל לקום על עמדו מגודל היראה
tags.why: Religious awe is the subject of the request and of its effect.

quotes: ולא יכל לקום על עמדו מגודל היראה
tags.why: The man is overwhelmed by fear and awe.

quotes: והוריד הרב בידו ונפל אותו האיש על פניו ארצה
tags.why: The rebbe's hand gesture works a supernatural effect on the man's body.

quotes: ששאל אחד את הה״צ מו״ר מוה׳ זושא
tags.why: A seeker comes to the tsaddik with a request for instruction.

quotes: עד שהניף הרב ידו אז קם על עמדו
tags.why: Shows the tsaddik's power to act upon another person's spiritual state.
A teaching encounter between the master and a would-be disciple.

missing_concepts: the tsaddik transmitting a spiritual state (awe) to another person by bodily gesture
